en-US.description: Local-first music player with Hi-Res audio, AutoMix, word-synced lyrics, smart playlists, themes and plugins. No account or subscription.
en-US.longDescription:
WaveFlow is a local-first music player for Windows, macOS and Linux. It scans your music folders, organizes everything by album, artist and genre, and plays it through its own real-time audio engine. No account, no subscription, no streaming service: your music stays on your machine.

It plays Hi-Res files, DSD and 5.1 / 7.1 on the speakers they name, with gapless playback, crossfades and AutoMix on the beat, ReplayGain, an equalizer and exclusive output. It adds lyrics synced word by word with a lyrics editor, smart playlists, Daily Mix and Release Radar, a tag workshop and MusicBrainz enrichment with undo, WebDAV and SMB shares, podcasts, six skins and fourteen themes, Last.fm and ListenBrainz, DLNA and MPD servers, and sandboxed plugins, in 17 languages.
en-US.name: WaveFlow
en-US.releaseNotes:
WaveFlow 2.0.0
WaveFlow 2.0 — A new look. Still your music. New logo. New interface. A new wave.
WaveFlow 2.0 is here, and it is the biggest release I have made: a new look and a new logo, a new interface, an audio engine that plays 5.1 and 7.1 on the right speakers, WebDAV and SMB shares, podcasts, a tag workshop, and a library that can fill its own gaps from MusicBrainz. Every one of its seventeen languages has now been read by a native speaker, and in Arabic the whole interface reads right to left. The fixes that already reached you in 1.9.2 to 1.9.8 are in here too, but they are not listed again.
On the beta? 2.0.0 is offered to you as an update, and the changes since beta.1 are under Since the beta. Once it is installed you can turn Settings → Maintenance → Updates → Beta channel off to stay on stable releases.
WaveFlow's Home in the Fluid skin: the track to pick up where you left off beside its cover, what plays next, and the suggestion of the day
⚠️ Before you update
2.0 upgrades your library's database the first time it opens it. Before it does, WaveFlow writes a copy of the database next to it and reads it back to check it. If that copy cannot be made or does not check out, nothing is migrated until you choose: try again, continue without a backup, or quit. (#946)
1.9 cannot open a library that 2.0 has upgraded — it will say the library was made by a newer version. If you want a way back, export your profile first from Settings → Storage and backups → Profile backups → Export.
🎨 A new interface
- Fluid is the new default. Navigation on a rail, a Home rebuilt around what you are listening to — where you left off, what plays next, and a suggestion of the day with the reason it was picked — the cover's light behind the music, and one side panel with Details, Lyrics and Queue as tabs. (#924, #904)
- Five materials on that layout: Fluid, Liquid (aurora glass), Pulse (neon), Editorial (a broadsheet on paper) and Lounge (a listening room lit by the record). Studio keeps the classic layout, now flat and precise, and stays the light choice for a machine without graphics acceleration. (#928, #930, #951, #952, #1036)
- Coming from 1.9, you open where you were: 1.9 saved your skin, so if you never changed it you start in Studio. The first page of the What's new panel takes you to Settings → Appearance → Skin.
- Visual effects: Automatic, Full or Reduced. Reduced draws every surface flat so the interface stays smooth without a GPU; Automatic, the default, chooses it on such a machine. (#957)
- Your own accent colour over any of the fourteen themes, or the colour of the playing track's cover. (#895)
- Theater mode for a screen across the room: the immersive view full screen and scaled up, the tracklist beside the cover, controls that fade, and the display kept on while music plays. Off by default; the TV button in the immersive view turns it on. (#970)
- The audio quality strip speaks plainly, and is now on by default under the player bar; its popover shows each stage the sound goes through and what it does to it. A Lossless badge joins Hi-Res and DSD. If you had turned the strip off, it stays off. (#1035, #1048)
- A new mark, the W of the name drawn as a wave, on the app icon; on the rail it breathes while music plays. (#953)
- Settings as groups of cards, with a count of what you changed on each page and a reset. Extensions is now a page of its own in the sidebar. (#959, #947)
- A What's new panel opens once after an update, with a "Try it" for each feature; new installs get a first-run journey instead; and a profile can have a picture. (#1000, #999, #1042)
- Pin albums, artists and playlists to the sidebar. (#962)
- Linux: a GNOME-style window frame as a choice under Wayland, and the desktop's own file pickers. (#960, #971)
The same page switching from Fluid to Liquid, Pulse, Editorial, Lounge and Studio while the same track plays
🌍 Seventeen languages, read by native speakers
- Every language was read by a native speaker before this release, and the wording they asked for is in: clearer sentences, the right plural forms, and the terms each language really uses. European Portuguese now counts like Portugal does ("0 canais", not "0 canal"). (#1063)
- In Arabic, the whole interface reads right to left: the sidebar and the rail move to the right, menus open toward the left and stay inside the window, arrows and chevrons turn around, and step numbers sit on the right side of their labels. What has a direction of its own keeps it: the progress bar and its times, previous / play / next, the volume and the other audio sliders, the charts and the equaliser curve. (#1064)
🎚️ The audio engine
- 5.1 and 7.1, on the speakers they name. Every channel is now routed by speaker, not by number, so a surround file plays on the right speakers, and one with more channels than you have is folded down by the broadcast standard (ITU-R BS.775) — quieter rather than distorted. On Linux, shared output opens at your sink's full width instead of stopping at stereo. Multichannel AAC files that were listed but would not play now play, and HE-AAC keeps its upper band. (#1009, #1012)
- WavPack and Monkey's Audio play, seek, get analysed and have their tags edited like a FLAC. (#1016)
- Speed without the chipmunk. At any speed, the pitch now stays where it is (the old behaviour is still an option), and you can transpose by up to 12 semitones either way. (#1020)
- AutoMix lands each crossfade on the beats of both tracks, and lets an album play through without fading. Off by default, in Settings → Audio → Track transitions; it needs a crossfade length and analysed tracks, and falls back to the usual fade otherwise. (#993)
- Balance and stereo width, which leave the sound bit-perfect at their neutral values. (#949)
- Test your output: a beep on the left, the right, then both — or on each speaker of a surround setup — with the format the device really runs at, in Settings → Audio → Audio output. (#888)
- An EQ boost no longer clips on a loud master, and 16-bit exclusive output is dithered instead of rounded. (#906)
- The spectrum follows the sound you hear, without trembling, and quiet passages stay quiet. (#1043, #890)
- Play files without importing them: drop them on "Play now", press Ctrl+O, or use your system's Open with (WaveFlow makes itself the default for nothing). QuickPlay can also hand its queue over at the same spot. (#927, #929, #931, #942)
- Pause live radio for up to 30 minutes and catch up, HLS stations play, and Ogg stations show the song's title. (#972, #1021)
- Autoplay keeps the music going with related tracks from your library when the queue ends. Off by default. (#949)
📚 Library
- WebDAV and SMB shares as library folders, read without the system mounting them, from Settings → Storage and backups → Folders and caches. Read-only, streamed through a local cache (5 GB by default), and a share that is away greys its tracks out instead of losing them. SMB 2 and 3 only. (#1007)
- A Quality tab sorts your files by what their audio says, and flags lossless files that appear to come from a lossy source. Track properties can show the spectrogram behind the verdict. (#1038, #886, #964)
- Replace a file with a better copy and keep its plays, likes and playlists. Deleting duplicates moves them to the trash, so a rescan no longer brings them back. (#887, #879, closes #878)
- Analysis reads more of the music: a tempo that knows when it is unsure, an energy measure, the key when no tag gives one, and where the beats fall. Daily Mix now sorts by energy. The next analysis pass measures again the tracks 1.9 had analysed. (#864, #865, #877, #882)
- An album page names its missing tracks, and album artist and composer can now be edited. (#948)
- The scanner stops guessing wrong: an unplugged drive no longer hides its tracks, every credited artist is read, two albums that share a title are no longer merged into Various Artists, a moved file keeps its history, and a file with deeply nested chapter frames no longer crashes the scan. (#1022, #1033)
- Dropped files are copied into a WaveFlow folder in your Music folder, instead of adding the folder they came from. (#929)
- Also: ratings survive a rescan, format filters find Ogg, ALAC and DSD files, a track on a NAS no longer cuts off the one playing before it, and single-click play works in every list. (#1010, #1011, #926, #935)
🏷️ Tags, enrichment and Release Radar
The tag workshop edits the tags of an album, a folder or a selection in one table: fill, find and replace (regex included), change case, renumber, or start from a MusicBrainz release. Nothing is written before you have seen every change, field by field, and every batch can be undone — a file changed since is left alone. (#992)
The tag workshop's preview before writing an album matched on MusicBrainz: for each file, every changed field shown before and after
- Library enrichment fills what is missing — genres, release dates, credits, covers, artist facts — from MusicBrainz, in WaveFlow's database only, never in your files. Doubtful matches wait for your review, and all of it can be undone. Off by default, because it sends album titles and artist names to MusicBrainz: Settings → Library → Enrichment. (#983)
- Release Radar is built in: recent releases by the artists in your library, with what you already own gathered in a playlist. It takes the place of the Release Radar extension in the sidebar. (#987)
- Adding a cover or longer tags to a FLAC works. An edit that outgrew the file's reserved space used to be refused. (#1031)
🎤 Lyrics
- A lyrics editor rebuilt from scratch, in three steps: edit, sync by line or by word with the space bar while the song plays, then check the result. Singers, backing vocals, translations and romanization, saved as LRC, Enhanced LRC or TTML — and a .ttml file next to a track is now read. (#994, #949)
- Share a lyrics excerpt as an image card. (#962)
